channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: WriteFreely patches critical authentication and federation flaws
item.description: WriteFreely 0.17.3 fixes an authentication bypass that could let an unauthenticated attacker use the API as another user. The open-source blogging release also closes private-content exposure through ActivityPub, a WebFinger request flaw and several access-control problems; administrators are urged to update.

item.title: WordPress Credits passes 50 participating institutions
item.description: More than 50 colleges and universities across 17 countries now award academic recognition for contributing to WordPress. The free program pairs students with mentors on translation, documentation, learning materials, development and testing; its dashboard counted 364 graduates by Oct. 19.

item.title: Spreaker pledges safeguards against unauthorized podcast copies
item.description: After Podnews documented copied shows on Spreaker, the Triton Digital platform committed to changes aimed at stopping unauthorized imports and protecting creators. The development turns scrutiny of podcast copying into a concrete response and renewed attention to feed ownership.

item.title: RSS.com expands video podcasting through open feed enclosures
item.description: RSS.com says its HLS video service now carries video through Apple Podcasts and supporting Podcasting 2.0 apps while preserving audio playback elsewhere. Video is placed in the RSS feed as an alternate enclosure, with supported apps including Pocket Casts, Fountain, TrueFans and Podcast Guru.

item.title: Transistor keeps podcast feeds readable without XSLT
item.description: Transistor rebuilt the browser presentation of its podcast RSS feeds with CSS ahead of Chrome's planned removal of XSLT. The new view retains cover art, show information, the feed URL and episode listings, offering a practical way for human-readable feeds to survive a browser-platform change.

item.title: Salon ceases publication after 31 years on the web
item.description: Salon has stopped publishing after a 31-year run that began when original online journalism was still an experiment. The publication said the economics of independent digital media made its model unsustainable, closing a site whose politics, culture, criticism and essays helped define web-native magazines.

item.title: Awesome Motive acquires Drip and Sleeknote
item.description: Awesome Motive's WPBeginner Growth Fund acquired email and SMS platform Drip and conversion tool Sleeknote. The companies will remain an independent unit under Mogens Møller, while tighter connections with WPForms and MemberPress are planned. Drip says more than 6,000 brands use its service.

item.title: Independent Podcast Awards honor a hyperlocal bus show
item.description: Great Days Out on the Bus from Buxton won 2026 Independent Podcast of the Year, plus travel and artwork honors. Solo producer Maria Passingham's sound-rich local show led a 28-category program celebrating work made outside major networks; more than 400 people attended the London ceremony.

item.title: WordPress Studio rebuilds its desktop workspace
item.description: WordPress Studio's redesigned free desktop app puts sites, chats and live previews in one workspace, with unified settings and command access. It supports macOS, Windows and Linux, keeps development local, offers shareable preview links and exposes the same workflow through a command-line interface.

item.title: AT Protocol brings Jetstream semantics to private Spaces
item.description: AT Protocol says its forthcoming Spaces system will work with existing Jetstream clients through a familiar replay-then-live stream. Self-hosted sync services will borrow short-lived access from authorized users and deliver permitted records without a public relay, reducing the split between public and non-public app development.

item.title: Archive-It updates its guide to the CDX/C index
item.description: Archive-It's revised guide explains how to query its Wayback index by URL, collection and date range, select or collapse fields, and locate captures in WARC storage. The documentation is a practical route to auditing web-archive coverage and retrieving capture metadata without relying only on the calendar interface.

item.title: Firefox roadmap adds offline reading and local speech recognition
item.description: Mozilla's updated Firefox roadmap includes a floating Mini Window, read-aloud and offline reading, local speech recognition that keeps audio on the device, site-specific VPN rules and a toolbar control for clearing browsing data. The browser's built-in PDF viewer also now starts up to 45% faster on desktop.

item.title: Chrome 157 release notes put XSLT removal on the near horizon
item.description: Chrome's Nov. 4 enterprise notes reiterate that browser support for XSLT is being removed, with stable releases scheduled to stop processing it on Nov. 17 outside approved extensions. That change matters for XML feeds and other documents that still depend on client-side stylesheets for readable browser presentation.

item.title: What would less polarizing political journalism look like?
item.description: Joy Mayer, Mónica Guzmán and Jonathan Stray examine how political reporting can serve people across a divided electorate without laundering misinformation. Their discussion addresses ideological gaps between newsrooms and audiences, the limits of both-sides framing, curiosity, accountability and hiring for broader viewpoints.

item.title: Safari Technology Preview 256 improves accessibility and web interoperability
item.description: WebKit's latest preview fixes list markers and nested frames for assistive technology, aligns enhanced select styles with other browsers and corrects multiple SVG sizing failures. It also expands canvas text controls and adds security diagnostics for cross-origin isolation.
